title: Properties of triangles, quadrilaterals and regular polygons
summary: Use angle, side, diagonal and symmetry properties of common shapes.
objectives: Use angle and side properties of triangles and special quadrilaterals.
Determine line and rotational symmetry of regular polygons and quadrilaterals.
Combine shape properties to solve multi-step angle problems.

blocks.text: Triangles have interior-angle sum 180°. Special quadrilaterals are distinguished by parallel sides, equal sides, right angles and diagonal properties. A regular polygon has equal sides and equal angles, with rotational order and number of symmetry lines equal to its number of sides.

Shape properties come from definitions and markings. A triangle totals 180°. A quadrilateral totals 360°. Isosceles triangles have two equal sides and two equal base angles. Equilateral triangles have three equal sides and three 60° angles. Regular polygons have all sides and all interior angles equal.

For a multi-step problem, record every justified property beside the diagram: equal sides, equal angles, parallel sides and symmetry. Then use triangle or quadrilateral angle sums. A diagonal can split a quadrilateral into triangles, but properties of the diagonal depend on the quadrilateral type.

sections.title: Worked example

prompt.text: An isosceles triangle has equal angles of 64°. Find its remaining angle.

sections.verification_note: The result follows the stated property and satisfies the original geometric conditions.

sections.title: Worked example: apply the method

prompt.text: An isosceles trapezium has two equal angles of 68° on one base. Find the two angles on the other base.

content.text: Adjacent interior angles between the parallel bases are supplementary.
Each angle on the other base is 180°−68°=112°.

sections.verification_note: The four angles total 360° and the base-angle pairs are equal.

blocks.text: Do not assume a property merely because a drawing looks symmetric. Use stated markings and definitions. A regular polygon requires both equal sides and equal angles. When a diagonal is drawn, identify which new triangles and angle sums it creates.

prompt.text: What is the rotational order of a regular hexagon?

feedback.text: A regular hexagon matches itself six times in one complete turn.

blocks.text: Name the relevant property, write the complete angle or construction relationship, calculate carefully, and check that every angle and length is geometrically possible.
Before moving on, explain the relevant property in words, show the equation or formula with units, and use the diagram markings to check that every correspondence is consistent.
